subject: Partial invariance: Identifying parameters to free up from reviewing variances of parameter estimates across groups

messages.author: b1e2ae48042fca9f
messages.subject: Partial invariance: Identifying parameters to free up from reviewing variances of parameter estimates across groups
parts:
As I've mentioned elsewhere in this group, I have a large WLSMV model using 7 groups, 5 factors and 21 indicators. The use of lavtestscore() fails to converge and so I can't use that to identify which parameters to free up in order to see if partial scalar invariance can be pursued.

If I look at the parameter estimates of the thresholds (there are 163 x 7 groups!) and take the standard deviation of each threshold across the 7 grous, and then sort from small to large, does a small standard deviation indicate that the threshold parameter can be constrained across the groups? Or am I completely barking up the wrong tree here?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Partial invariance: Identifying parameters to free up from reviewing variances of parameter estimates across groups
parts: am I completely barking up the wrong tree here?

Yes, wrong tree.  Did you consider the MIMIC approach I suggested on another thread?  It assumes invariance of everything (single-group model), but you can test (only) for differences in intercepts by regressing (some) indicators on group dummy codes.  This article discusses it for IRT, which is analogous to item factor analysis.

https://doi.org/10.1080/00273170802620121
